summary: Replaced animation-only pathway labels and formats with project-native documentary routes.
priorBasis: The prior reusable pathway template incorrectly injected animation directions even though the card identifies the project as a documentary film.

projectProfile.qualification: The published card identifies the current format as a documentary film, while cited public sources describe its festival recognition, theatrical release, production context, and campaign.

pathways.label: Festival and theatrical expansion
pathways.audience: Festival programmers, specialty exhibitors, cultural-documentary audiences, and viewers interested in Chicano history.
pathways.rationale: The cited festival awards and public recognition support testing additional documentary exhibition opportunities without treating awards as proof of audience demand.
strengths: The existing feature has cited festival recognition that can make outreach more legible.
A completed documentary can be evaluated without changing its medium.
risks: Festival recognition may not convert into additional bookings or sustained attendance.
Current rights, windows, and exhibition availability remain unverified.
openQuestions: Which territories and exhibition windows are currently available?
Which prior screenings produced reusable programmer or audience feedback?

nextExperiment.title: Documentary exhibitor fit interviews
nextExperiment.hypothesis: A concise evidence-linked exhibition packet will reveal which venues see a credible fit for the existing feature.
nextExperiment.method: Share one bounded packet and screener-access request with a small set of documentary programmers and specialty exhibitors.
nextExperiment.participantAction: Review the packet and identify fit, timing, and the main booking constraint.
nextExperiment.signal: Repeated fit themes and qualified requests for a follow-up conversation or screener.

pathways.label: Public media and educational licensing
pathways.format: Feature documentary broadcast and educational licensing
pathways.audience: Public-media viewers, educators, libraries, cultural institutions, and students of Chicano history and theater.
pathways.rationale: The cited production context, historical footage, and interviews support testing documentary broadcast and classroom use while rights and partner commitments remain unconfirmed.
strengths: The documented subject matter and interview material can support facilitated educational discussion.
The cited production context gives public-media outreach a relevant starting point.
risks: Educational use may require additional clearances, captions, guides, or license administration.
Production involvement does not establish current broadcast or licensing commitments.
openQuestions: Which educational rights and accessibility assets are already available?
Which course areas and institutional buyers have the clearest documented fit?

nextExperiment.title: Educational use-case review
nextExperiment.hypothesis: A documentary discussion guide and rights summary will reveal the most credible classroom and institutional uses.
nextExperiment.method: Present a bounded sample guide and licensing outline to a small group of educators, librarians, and cultural-program staff.
nextExperiment.participantAction: Identify a concrete use case, required materials, and the main adoption constraint.
nextExperiment.signal: Repeated use cases and qualified requests for screening or licensing information.

pathways.label: Community impact screenings
pathways.audience: Chicano cultural organizations, community hosts, campaign supporters, local arts groups, and intergenerational audiences.
pathways.rationale: The cited campaign and documentary subject matter support testing host-led community screenings without assuming that campaign backing equals current participation.
strengths: The campaign provides a public starting point for identifying potential community hosts.
The documentary's cultural-history focus can support facilitated local conversations.
risks: Past campaign participation does not prove present host capacity or attendance.
Community exhibition requires clear rights, logistics, accessibility, and facilitation support.
openQuestions: Which campaign supporters or cultural organizations still want to host screenings?
What minimum toolkit would let a host run an accessible and rights-compliant event?

nextExperiment.title: Community host interest pilot
nextExperiment.hypothesis: A clear host toolkit will reveal whether a small group can organize rights-compliant documentary screenings.
nextExperiment.method: Share one draft host kit with a bounded set of campaign-connected and cultural-community contacts.
nextExperiment.participantAction: State a preferred venue, date range, audience, and the support needed to host.
nextExperiment.signal: Qualified host plans that name a venue path, timing, and unresolved requirement.
